sites.rationale: The ledger (L1/L2/L3/L4) reports an anti-FLAG tag added to the N-terminus of the full-length, membrane-anchored M5 mAChR. The canonical topology places residues 1–29 extracellular with TM1 beginning at residue 30; a prepend (insert_after_residue=0) places the tag 30 residues from the TM1 boundary, well above the ≥3-residue minimum. No specific junction residue is named in the paper, but the N-terminus is the only extracellular terminus of a GPCR and the only location consistent with the description; position is therefore topology-derived. The exogenous HA signal sequence drives surface trafficking and is cleaved, leaving the FLAG tag exposed on the extracellular face. Modified full-length M5 mAChR construct used for cryo-EM structural and functional studies: ICL3 residues 237–421 removed, exogenous HA signal sequence added, and anti-FLAG epitope tag incorporated at the N-terminus. Construct expressed in mammalian cells and used for receptor pharmacology and structure determination.

sources.claim: A modified M 5 mAChR construct was used where residues 237–421 of ICL3 were removed and HA signal sequence and anti-Flag epitope tag were added to the N terminus.

literature_notes: L1, L2, L3, and L4 all describe the same N-terminal FLAG-tagged M5 construct (two papers citing the same engineering strategy); L1 is used as the primary supporting clip. L5 describes a T4 lysozyme insertion replacing ICL3 residues 225–430, which is entirely within the large intracellular loop 3 (topology: 215–443 intracellular) and therefore does not qualify as a surface tag site. The ICL3 deletion (residues 237–421) in L1–L4 is likewise intracellular and is recorded in other_positions. No ledger line supports an insertion in any of the short extracellular loops (ECL1: 88–104, ECL2: 170–191, ECL3: 465–478) or the C-terminal intracellular tail.
